nodes.summary: Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then $f_1 f_2 f_3 f_6 f_9^2 f_{18}^2 = f_6^2 f_9^6 - q f_3 f_6 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 - 2 q^2 f_3^2 f_{18}^6$.
nodes.title: 3-dissection of $f_1 f_2$

nodes.summary: Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then $f_2 f_3^8 f_{18}^3 = f_1^2 f_6^4 f_9^6 + 2 q f_1^2 f_3 f_6^3 f_9^3 f_{18}^3 + 4 q^2 f_1^2 f_3^2 f_6^2 f_{18}^6$.
nodes.title: 3-dissection of $f_2 / f_1^2$

nodes.summary: Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then $f_2^2 f_3 f_9 f_{18} = f_1 f_6 f_9^3 + q f_1 f_3 f_{18}^3$.
nodes.title: 3-dissection of $f_2^2 / f_1$

nodes.summary: Let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$ denote the Euler products in $\mathbb{Z}[[q]]$. Then $f_2^2 f_3^3 f_4 f_{12} - q f_1 f_2^2 f_{12}^4 = f_1 f_4^4 f_6^2$.
nodes.title: 2-dissection of $f_3^3 / f_1$

nodes.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the PEND condition when no even number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every even part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the even parts are not distinct.
nodes.title: The PEND condition

nodes.summary: The multisets of parts $\{1, 1\}$ and $\{2\}$ satisfy the POND condition, while $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 1\}$ do not; the multisets $\{1\}$ and $\{2, 2\}$ satisfy the PEND condition, while $\{2\}$ and $\{2, 4\}$ do not.
nodes.title: Examples of POND and PEND parts

nodes.summary: A multiset $s$ of natural numbers (the parts of a partition) satisfies the POND condition when no odd number occurs in $s$ exactly once; equivalently, every odd part that occurs in $s$ has multiplicity at least $2$, so the odd parts are not distinct.
nodes.title: The POND condition

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series in $q$, $f_1 f_4 f_6 \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12}$. This is the identity $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pend}(n) q^n = f_2 f_{12} / (f_1 f_4 f_6)$ with the denominator cleared.
nodes.title: Generating function for PEND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$, $\mathrm{pend}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (17 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} - 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for PEND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(27n + 10) \equiv \mathrm{pend}(3n + 1) \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pend}(m)$ be the number of PEND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(27n + 19) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: Congruence modulo 3 for PEND partitions of 27n + 19

nodes.summary: The number of PEND partitions of $0$ is $1$, that is, $\mathrm{pend}(0) = 1$.
nodes.title: PEND partitions of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pend}(n)$ is the number of PEND partitions of $n$: partitions of $n$ in which every even part that occurs appears at least twice (OEIS A265254).
nodes.title: The PEND partition function

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \equiv 0 \pmod{2}$, $\mathrm{pond}(27n + 26) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$ and $\mathrm{pond}(3n + 1) \equiv 0 \pmod{4}$.
nodes.title: Congruences modulo 2, 3 and 4 for POND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ be the number of POND partitions of $n$, and let $f_k = \prod_{m \ge 1} (1 - q^{km})$. Then, as integer power series in $q$, $f_2^2 f_3 f_{12} \sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2$. This is the identity $\sum_{n \ge 0} \mathrm{pond}(n) q^n = f_4 f_6^2 / (f_2^2 f_3 f_{12})$ with the denominator cleared.
nodes.title: Generating function for POND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For all natural numbers $\alpha \ge 1$ and $n$, $\mathrm{pond}\left(3^{2\alpha+1} n + (23 \cdot 3^{2\alpha} + 1)/8\right) \equiv 0 \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: Infinite family of congruences modulo 3 for POND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $\mathrm{pond}(m)$ be the number of POND partitions of $m$. For every natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(27n + 17) \equiv \mathrm{pond}(3n + 2) \pmod{3}$.
nodes.title: Internal congruence modulo 3 for POND partitions

nodes.summary: The number $\mathrm{pond}(0)$ of POND partitions of $0$ equals $1$: the only partition of $0$ is the empty partition, and it is POND.
nodes.title: The number of POND partitions of zero

nodes.summary: For a natural number $n$, $\mathrm{pond}(n)$ is the number of partitions of $n$ that are POND, that is, in which every odd part that occurs has multiplicity at least $2$ (OEIS A265256).
nodes.title: Number of POND partitions

nodes.summary: Let $p$ be a prime, let $j, k, m \ge 1$ be natural numbers, and let $f_m = \prod_{i \ge 1} (1 - q^{mi})$. Then for every natural number $n$, the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_m^{p^j k}$ is congruent modulo $p^j$ to the coefficient of $q^n$ in $f_{pm}^{p^{j-1} k}$.
nodes.title: Prime-power congruence for powers of Euler products

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
